(Surat al-Dukhan)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night; indeed, We were ever warning.﴾ ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct,﴾ ﴿a command from Us. Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers],﴾ ﴿as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain.﴾ ﴿There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.﴾ ﴿Rather, they are in doubt, playing.﴾
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night; indeed, We were ever warning.﴾ ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct,﴾ ﴿a command from Us. Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers],﴾ ﴿as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain.﴾ ﴿There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.﴾ ﴿Rather, they are in doubt, playing.﴾, and in the verse there are issues:

The first issue: concerning His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ there are several possibilities:
The first: the intended meaning is: this is ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾, like your saying: "This is Zayd, by Allah."
The second: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾, and then it is said: ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down.﴾
The third: the intended meaning is: Ha, Mim, by the Book that makes things clear, indeed We sent it down; so this is, in effect, two oaths upon one thing.

The second issue: They said: this indicates that the Qur'an is created (ḥudūth), for several reasons:
The first: His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾, its meaning being: this is Ha, Mim, meaning this is a thing composed of these letters, and what is composed of successive letters is created (muḥdath).
The second: it is established that swearing by these things is not valid, but rather by the Lord of these things; so the meaning is: "By the Lord of Ha, Mim and the Lord of the Clear Book." And whoever is a created being under lordship is created.
The third: He described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from gathering (jam'), so its meaning is that it is gathered, and what is gathered is subject to the handling of others, and whatever is so is created.
The fourth: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, and what is sent down is subject to the handling of others (page 203), and whatever is so is created. We have mentioned many times that all these proofs indicate that a thing composed of successive letters and consecutive sounds is created, and knowledge of this is necessary and self-evident; none disputes it except one who lacks reason and does not know the meaning of the eternal and the created. And if that is so, how could one dispute the soundness of these proofs? What has been established as eternal is something other than what is composed of these letters and sounds.

The third issue: It is possible that by "the Book" here is meant the earlier scriptures which God sent down to His prophets, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39], and He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Qur'an; and on this reading He swears by the Qur'an that He sent it down during a blessed night. This kind of speech indicates the utmost glorification of the Qur'an, just as a man may say, when he wishes to exalt a person from whom he needs something: "I seek your intercession with yourself, and I swear by your right over you."

The fourth issue: ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the Clear) is that which includes the explanation of what people need in their religion and their worldly affairs. He described it as "making clear," although the true act of making clear belongs to God, because the clarification was achieved through it, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76], and He said in another verse: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and He said: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate?﴾ [al-Rum: 35]. Thus He described it with speech, since it is the utmost in clarification, so it is as though it were a tongue that speaks; and the purpose in this is to exaggerate its description with this meaning.

The fifth issue: They differed concerning this blessed night. Most said it is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). ʿIkrimah and another group said it is the Night of Acquittal (Laylat al-Bara'a), which is the night of the middle of Sha'ban. As for the first group, they argued for the soundness of their view with several points:
The first: He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1], and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So it must be that this blessed night is that which is called the Night of Power, lest there be contradiction.
The second: He said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], thus clarifying that the sending down of the Qur'an occurred in the month of Ramadan; and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So this blessed night must fall in the month of Ramadan, and everyone who said this blessed night falls in Ramadan said it is the Night of Power; thus it is established that it is the Night of Power.
The third: He said describing the Night of Power: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 4–5]. He also said here: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾, which is appropriate to His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿by permission of their Lord concerning every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 5]. When the descriptions are close, it is necessary to say that one of the two nights is the other.
The fourth: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated in his Tafsir from Qatadah that he said: "The scrolls of Ibrahim were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah on the sixth night of it, the Psalms on the twelfth night that had passed of it, the Gospel on the eighteenth night that had passed of it, and the Qur'an on the twenty-fourth night that had passed of Ramadan; and the blessed night is the Night of Power."
The fifth: The Night of Power was named so because its worth (qadr) and nobility with God is great. It is known that its worth and nobility are not due to that time itself, because time is one thing in its essence and attributes, so it is impossible for some part of it to be more noble than another in its essence. Thus it is established that its nobility and worth are due to the fact that great noble matters occurred in it, which have great worth and a lofty rank. It is known that the rank of religion is higher and greater than the rank of this world, and the highest and most noble of things in religion in rank is the Qur'an, because through it the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ was established, and through it the distinction between truth and falsehood became manifest in all the other revealed books of God, as He said describing it: ("and a guardian over it" [al-Ma'idah: 48]), and through it the degrees of the people of felicity and the depths of the people of wretchedness became manifest. Accordingly, nothing is greater in worth, higher in mention, or greater in rank than the Qur'an. So if its descent had occurred in another night besides the Night of Power, then the Night of Power would be this second night, not the first. And since they agreed that the Night of Power which falls in Ramadan is the one, we know that the Qur'an was sent down in that night.

As for those who say that the blessed night mentioned in this verse is the middle night of Sha'ban, I have not seen for them any proof to rely upon; they have been content merely to transmit it from some people. If there is a saying from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning it, then there is nothing more to be said; otherwise the truth is the first view. Then these proponents of this view claim that the middle night of Sha'ban has four names: the Blessed Night, the Night of Acquittal, the Night of the Decree (Laylat al-Sakk), and the Night of Mercy. It is also said that it was named the Night of Acquittal and the Night of the Decree because when the official (bunduar) collects the land tax from its people, he writes them an acquittal; likewise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes an acquittal for His believing servants on this night. It is also said: this night is specific to five qualities:
The first: the distinguishing of every wise matter therein, as He said: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾.
The second: the excellence of worship in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays one hundred units of prayer on this night, Allah sends to him one hundred angels: thirty to give him good news of Paradise, thirty to secure him from the punishment of the Fire, thirty to ward off the calamities of this world, and ten to ward off the schemes of Satan."
The third quality: the descent of mercy. He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah shows mercy to my community on this night in number equal to the hair of the sheep of the Banu Kalb."
The fourth quality: the attainment of forgiveness. He ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, forgives all Muslims on that night, except a soothsayer, or a person harboring enmity, or a habitual drinker of wine, or one who is disobedient to his parents, or one who persists in fornication."
The fifth quality: that God gave His Messenger on this night the complete intercession. That is, he asked on the thirteenth night of Sha'ban for his community, and was given a third of it; then he asked on the fourteenth night and was given two-thirds; then he asked on the fifteenth night and was given all of it, except whoever fled from God as a camel flees.
I have transmitted this section from the *Kashshaf*. If it is said: there is no doubt that time is an expression for the extended duration whose measure is the motions of the spheres and the stars, and that in itself it is a thing whose parts are alike, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be better than others; and place is an expression for extended space and empty void, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be more noble than others; and if that is so, then specifying some of its parts with greater nobility over the rest is a preference of one side of a possibility over the other without a determining cause, and that is impossible. We say: the affirmation of the createdness of the world and the affirmation that its Agent is a free-choosing agent is based on this principle, namely that it is not improbable for a free-choosing agent to specify a particular time for bringing the world into being rather than what precedes or follows it. If this principle is refuted, then the createdness of the world is refuted and the free-choosing Agent is refuted, and then the discussion of the interpretation of the Qur'an would have no benefit. And if this principle is sound, then the question you raised is removed. This is the reliable answer. People have also said: it is not improbable that God specifies some times with greater honor, so that this becomes an incentive for the responsible person to undertake acts of obedience in that time. For this reason He made it clear that He concealed it among the times and did not specify it; for if it were not specific, the responsible person would suppose in every time that it might be that noble time, and this would move him to persist in acts of obedience at all times. When you reflect on this principle, it becomes clear to you that time and place only gained additional distinctions following the nobility of the human being, who is the principal, and everything else is subordinate to him. And God knows best.

Page 205
The sixth issue: It is narrated that ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥarūrī asked Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1] and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, how is this valid, given that Allah sent down the Qur'an in all the months? Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "O son of the black woman, if I die and this comes into your mind and you do not find its answer, you are ruined. The Qur'an descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the House of Honor (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), which is in the lowest heaven; then it descended afterward in various events, occasion by occasion." And God knows best.

* * *

The seventh issue: explaining the arrangement of these verses. Know that their purpose is the glorification of the Qur'an from three aspects:
The first: the explanation of the glorification of the Qur'an in terms of its own essence.
The second: the explanation of its glorification by reason of the nobility of the time in which it was sent down.

The third aspect: the explanation of its greatness in terms of the nobility of its rank.

As for the explanation of its greatness in terms of its essence, it has three aspects:

The first is that God Most High swore by it, and that indicates its nobility.

The second is that God Most High swore by it regarding its being sent down on a blessed night. We have mentioned that swearing by a thing with regard to one of its own states indicates that it is at the utmost level of nobility.

The third is that God Most High described it as being "clear" (mubin), and that also indicates its nobility in its essence.

As for the second type, which is the explanation of its nobility by virtue of the nobility of the time at which it was sent down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾. This is an alert that its being sent down on a blessed night requires its nobility and majesty. Then we say: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ requires two matters. One is that God Most High sent it down. The second is that this night is blessed. God then mentioned, after this statement, what serves as an explanation of each of the two. As for the explanation of why God Most High sent it down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever warners﴾, meaning that the wisdom in sending down this sura is that the warning of creation is not complete except by it. As for the explanation that this night is a blessed night, there are two matters. One is that God Most High makes every wise matter distinct therein. The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

As for the third type, it is the explanation of the nobility of the Qur'an by virtue of the nobility of its Sender. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾. He thus explained that this warning and sending were brought about only by God Most High. Then He explained that this sending was for the sake of perfecting mercy, which is His saying: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾. The expected phrasing would have been "as a mercy from Us," but He placed the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to signify that lordship (rububiyyah) requires mercy upon those who are nurtured. Then He explained that this mercy fell in accordance with the needs of those in need, because God Most High hears their supplications and knows the kinds of their needs. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This is what came to mind regarding how some of these verses are connected to others.

**Eighth issue: explaining the individual words of these expressions.**

As for His saying Most High: ﴿Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night﴾, it has been said regarding it that God Most High sent down the Qur'an in its entirety from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven on this night, and then He sent down at every time what the responsible person needs. It has also been said: the copying of that from the Preserved Tablet begins on the Night of Acquittal (laylat al-bara'ah), and the completion takes place on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Then the copy of provisions is handed to Mika'il, the copy of wars to Jibril, likewise earthquakes, thunderbolts and landslides, the copy of deeds to Isma'il, the lord of the lowest heaven, who is a great angel, and the copy of calamities to the Angel of Death.

Page 206

As for His saying Most High: ﴿wherein every wise matter is made distinct﴾, meaning, on that blessed night every wise matter is made distinct, that is, it is detailed and clarified, from their saying: "I separated the thing, I separate it, separation (farq) and criterion (furqan)." The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari's commentary) said: it is read as yufarriqu with shaddah, and as yafruqu with the verb ascribed to the agent and kull in the accusative. The one who distinguishes is God, Mighty and Majestic. Zayd ibn Ali read nufarriqu with the nun.

As for His saying: ﴿every wise matter﴾, al-hakim means "possessor of wisdom." This is because God Most High's assigning each person a specific state in terms of lifespan, provision, term, happiness and misery indicates His profound wisdom. Since those acts and decrees indicate the wisdom of their Doer, they are described as wise. This is a metaphorical attribution, because "wise" is in reality an attribute of the one who issues the command, and describing the matter as such is figurative. Then He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾. Regarding the accusative case of His saying ﴿amran﴾ there are two possibilities.

The first is that it is in the accusative by way of specification (ikhtisas). This is because God Most High explained the nobility of those decrees and rulings by describing them as wise, and then increased the explanation of their nobility by saying: "I mean by this matter a matter arising from Us, existing from Our presence, as Our knowledge and governance require."

The second is that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), and in this there are three possibilities:

The first is that it is a circumstantial state of one of the two pronouns in ﴿We sent it down﴾: either of the pronoun of the agent, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ issuing commands with a command, or of the pronoun of the object, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ while it is a command from Us with what must be done.

The third is what Abu Ali al-Farisi related from Abu al-Hasan, may God have mercy on them both: that he took His saying ﴿amran﴾ as a circumstantial state, and the qualified noun (dhu al-hal) is His saying ﴿every wise matter﴾, which is indefinite.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾, meaning: indeed We performed that warning only for the sake of "Indeed We were ever senders," meaning the prophets.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, meaning, for the sake of mercy, so it is in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning that this mercy was truly mercy, because those in need either mention their needs with their tongues or do not mention them. If they mention them, He Most High hears their speech and so knows their needs; and if they do not mention them, He Most High knows them. Thus it is established that His being (All-Hearing, All-Knowing) requires that He send down His mercy upon them.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are certain﴾. There are issues regarding this:

The first issue: Ibn Amir... — *[see note below]*

The first issue: Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "rabbi" with a kasrah on the ba' as an adjunct to His saying ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, while the rest read it with a dammah as an adjunct to His saying ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

The second issue: the purpose of this verse is that when the one who sends down is described with this majesty and greatness, what is sent down, which is the Qur'an, is at the utmost level of nobility and elevation.

The third issue: the benefit of His saying ﴿if you are certain﴾ is of several aspects:

The first: Abu Muslim said: its meaning is, if you seek certainty and desire it, then know that the matter is as We have said, like their saying: "So-and-so is a man of Najd and Tihamah," meaning he intends Najd and Tihamah.

The second: the author of al-Kashshaf said: they used to acknowledge that the heavens and the earth had a Lord and Creator, so it was said to them: the sending of messengers and the sending down of books is a mercy from the Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, then it was said: this is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, whom you acknowledge and admit to be the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if your acknowledgment is from knowledge and certainty, just as you say: "This is the bounty of Zayd, whose generosity people have heard of, if his report has reached you and you have heard his story." Then He Most High rejected that they were certain, by His saying: ﴿Nay, but they are in doubt, playing﴾, and that their acknowledgment does not proceed from knowledge and certainty, nor from earnestness and reality, but is a statement mixed with mockery and play. And God knows best.

The seventh issue: explaining the arrangement of these verses. Know that their purpose is the glorification of the Qur'an from three aspects:
The first: the explanation of the glorification of the Qur'an in terms of its own essence.
The second: the explanation of its glorification by reason of the nobility of the time in which it was sent down.

The third aspect: the explanation of its greatness in terms of the nobility of its rank.

As for the explanation of its greatness in terms of its essence, it has three aspects:

The first is that God Most High swore by it, and that indicates its nobility.

The second is that God Most High swore by it regarding its being sent down on a blessed night. We have mentioned that swearing by a thing with regard to one of its own states indicates that it is at the utmost level of nobility.

The third is that God Most High described it as being "clear" (mubin), and that also indicates its nobility in its essence.

As for the second type, which is the explanation of its nobility by virtue of the nobility of the time at which it was sent down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾. This is an alert that its being sent down on a blessed night requires its nobility and majesty. Then we say: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ requires two matters. One is that God Most High sent it down. The second is that this night is blessed. God then mentioned, after this statement, what serves as an explanation of each of the two. As for the explanation of why God Most High sent it down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever warners﴾, meaning that the wisdom in sending down this sura is that the warning of creation is not complete except by it. As for the explanation that this night is a blessed night, there are two matters. One is that God Most High makes every wise matter distinct therein. The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

Then He explained that this mercy fell in accordance with the needs of those in need, because God Most High hears their supplications and knows the kinds of their needs. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This is what came to mind regarding how some of these verses are connected to others.

It has also been said: the copying of that from the Preserved Tablet begins on the Night of Acquittal (laylat al-bara'ah), and the completion takes place on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Then the copy of provisions is handed to Mika'il, the copy of wars to Jibril, likewise earthquakes, thunderbolts and landslides, the copy of deeds to Isma'il, the lord of the lowest heaven, who is a great angel, and the copy of calamities to the Angel of Death.

Regarding the accusative case of His saying ﴿amran﴾ there are two possibilities.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night; indeed, We were ever warning.﴾ ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct,﴾ ﴿a command from Us. Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers],﴾ ﴿as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain.﴾ ﴿There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.﴾ ﴿Rather, they are in doubt, playing.﴾, and in the verse there are issues:

The first issue: concerning His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ there are several possibilities:
The first: the intended meaning is: this is ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾, like your saying: "This is Zayd, by Allah."
The second: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾, and then it is said: ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down.﴾
The third: the intended meaning is: Ha, Mim, by the Book that makes things clear, indeed We sent it down; so this is, in effect, two oaths upon one thing.

The second issue: They said: this indicates that the Qur'an is created (ḥudūth), for several reasons:
The first: His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾, its meaning being: this is Ha, Mim, meaning this is a thing composed of these letters, and what is composed of successive letters is created (muḥdath).
The second: it is established that swearing by these things is not valid, but rather by the Lord of these things; so the meaning is: "By the Lord of Ha, Mim and the Lord of the Clear Book." And whoever is a created being under lordship is created.
The third: He described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from gathering (jam'), so its meaning is that it is gathered, and what is gathered is subject to the handling of others, and whatever is so is created.
The fourth: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, and what is sent down is subject to the handling of others (page 203), and whatever is so is created. We have mentioned many times that all these proofs indicate that a thing composed of successive letters and consecutive sounds is created, and knowledge of this is necessary and self-evident; none disputes it except one who lacks reason and does not know the meaning of the eternal and the created. And if that is so, how could one dispute the soundness of these proofs? What has been established as eternal is something other than what is composed of these letters and sounds.

The third issue: It is possible that by "the Book" here is meant the earlier scriptures which God sent down to His prophets, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39], and He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Qur'an; and on this reading He swears by the Qur'an that He sent it down during a blessed night. This kind of speech indicates the utmost glorification of the Qur'an, just as a man may say, when he wishes to exalt a person from whom he needs something: "I seek your intercession with yourself, and I swear by your right over you."

The fourth issue: ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the Clear) is that which includes the explanation of what people need in their religion and their worldly affairs. He described it as "making clear," although the true act of making clear belongs to God, because the clarification was achieved through it, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76], and He said in another verse: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and He said: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate?﴾ [al-Rum: 35]. Thus He described it with speech, since it is the utmost in clarification, so it is as though it were a tongue that speaks; and the purpose in this is to exaggerate its description with this meaning.

The fifth issue: They differed concerning this blessed night. Most said it is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). ʿIkrimah and another group said it is the Night of Acquittal (Laylat al-Bara'a), which is the night of the middle of Sha'ban. As for the first group, they argued for the soundness of their view with several points:
The first: He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1], and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So it must be that this blessed night is that which is called the Night of Power, lest there be contradiction.
The second: He said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], thus clarifying that the sending down of the Qur'an occurred in the month of Ramadan; and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So this blessed night must fall in the month of Ramadan, and everyone who said this blessed night falls in Ramadan said it is the Night of Power; thus it is established that it is the Night of Power.
The third: He said describing the Night of Power: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 4–5]. He also said here: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾, which is appropriate to His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿by permission of their Lord concerning every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 5]. When the descriptions are close, it is necessary to say that one of the two nights is the other.
The fourth: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated in his Tafsir from Qatadah that he said: "The scrolls of Ibrahim were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah on the sixth night of it, the Psalms on the twelfth night that had passed of it, the Gospel on the eighteenth night that had passed of it, and the Qur'an on the twenty-fourth night that had passed of Ramadan; and the blessed night is the Night of Power."
The fifth: The Night of Power was named so because its worth (qadr) and nobility with God is great. It is known that its worth and nobility are not due to that time itself, because time is one thing in its essence and attributes, so it is impossible for some part of it to be more noble than another in its essence. Thus it is established that its nobility and worth are due to the fact that great noble matters occurred in it, which have great worth and a lofty rank. It is known that the rank of religion is higher and greater than the rank of this world, and the highest and most noble of things in religion in rank is the Qur'an, because through it the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ was established, and through it the distinction between truth and falsehood became manifest in all the other revealed books of God, as He said describing it: ("and a guardian over it" [al-Ma'idah: 48]), and through it the degrees of the people of felicity and the depths of the people of wretchedness became manifest. Accordingly, nothing is greater in worth, higher in mention, or greater in rank than the Qur'an. So if its descent had occurred in another night besides the Night of Power, then the Night of Power would be this second night, not the first. And since they agreed that the Night of Power which falls in Ramadan is the one, we know that the Qur'an was sent down in that night.

As for those who say that the blessed night mentioned in this verse is the middle night of Sha'ban, I have not seen for them any proof to rely upon; they have been content merely to transmit it from some people. If there is a saying from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning it, then there is nothing more to be said; otherwise the truth is the first view. Then these proponents of this view claim that the middle night of Sha'ban has four names: the Blessed Night, the Night of Acquittal, the Night of the Decree (Laylat al-Sakk), and the Night of Mercy. It is also said that it was named the Night of Acquittal and the Night of the Decree because when the official (bunduar) collects the land tax from its people, he writes them an acquittal; likewise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes an acquittal for His believing servants on this night. It is also said: this night is specific to five qualities:
The first: the distinguishing of every wise matter therein, as He said: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾.
The second: the excellence of worship in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays one hundred units of prayer on this night, Allah sends to him one hundred angels: thirty to give him good news of Paradise, thirty to secure him from the punishment of the Fire, thirty to ward off the calamities of this world, and ten to ward off the schemes of Satan."
The third quality: the descent of mercy. He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah shows mercy to my community on this night in number equal to the hair of the sheep of the Banu Kalb."
The fourth quality: the attainment of forgiveness. He ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, forgives all Muslims on that night, except a soothsayer, or a person harboring enmity, or a habitual drinker of wine, or one who is disobedient to his parents, or one who persists in fornication."
The fifth quality: that God gave His Messenger on this night the complete intercession. That is, he asked on the thirteenth night of Sha'ban for his community, and was given a third of it; then he asked on the fourteenth night and was given two-thirds; then he asked on the fifteenth night and was given all of it, except whoever fled from God as a camel flees.
I have transmitted this section from the *Kashshaf*. If it is said: there is no doubt that time is an expression for the extended duration whose measure is the motions of the spheres and the stars, and that in itself it is a thing whose parts are alike, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be better than others; and place is an expression for extended space and empty void, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be more noble than others; and if that is so, then specifying some of its parts with greater nobility over the rest is a preference of one side of a possibility over the other without a determining cause, and that is impossible. We say: the affirmation of the createdness of the world and the affirmation that its Agent is a free-choosing agent is based on this principle, namely that it is not improbable for a free-choosing agent to specify a particular time for bringing the world into being rather than what precedes or follows it. If this principle is refuted, then the createdness of the world is refuted and the free-choosing Agent is refuted, and then the discussion of the interpretation of the Qur'an would have no benefit. And if this principle is sound, then the question you raised is removed. This is the reliable answer. People have also said: it is not improbable that God specifies some times with greater honor, so that this becomes an incentive for the responsible person to undertake acts of obedience in that time. For this reason He made it clear that He concealed it among the times and did not specify it; for if it were not specific, the responsible person would suppose in every time that it might be that noble time, and this would move him to persist in acts of obedience at all times. When you reflect on this principle, it becomes clear to you that time and place only gained additional distinctions following the nobility of the human being, who is the principal, and everything else is subordinate to him. And God knows best.

The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

The third: the intended meaning is: Ha, Mim, by the Book that makes things clear, indeed We sent it down; so this is, in effect, two oaths upon one thing.

The second issue: They said: this indicates that the Qur'an is created (ḥudūth), for several reasons:
The first: His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾, its meaning being: this is Ha, Mim, meaning this is a thing composed of these letters, and what is composed of successive letters is created (muḥdath).
The second: it is established that swearing by these things is not valid, but rather by the Lord of these things; so the meaning is: "By the Lord of Ha, Mim and the Lord of the Clear Book." And whoever is a created being under lordship is created.
The third: He described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from gathering (jam'), so its meaning is that it is gathered, and what is gathered is subject to the handling of others, and whatever is so is created.
The fourth: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, and what is sent down is subject to the handling of others (page 203), and whatever is so is created. We have mentioned many times that all these proofs indicate that a thing composed of successive letters and consecutive sounds is created, and knowledge of this is necessary and self-evident; none disputes it except one who lacks reason and does not know the meaning of the eternal and the created. And if that is so, how could one dispute the soundness of these proofs? What has been established as eternal is something other than what is composed of these letters and sounds.

The third issue: It is possible that by "the Book" here is meant the earlier scriptures which God sent down to His prophets, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39], and He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Qur'an; and on this reading He swears by the Qur'an that He sent it down during a blessed night. This kind of speech indicates the utmost glorification of the Qur'an, just as a man may say, when he wishes to exalt a person from whom he needs something: "I seek your intercession with yourself, and I swear by your right over you."

The fourth issue: ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the Clear) is that which includes the explanation of what people need in their religion and their worldly affairs. He described it as "making clear," although the true act of making clear belongs to God, because the clarification was achieved through it, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76], and He said in another verse: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and He said: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate?﴾ [al-Rum: 35]. Thus He described it with speech, since it is the utmost in clarification, so it is as though it were a tongue that speaks; and the purpose in this is to exaggerate its description with this meaning.

The fifth issue: They differed concerning this blessed night. Most said it is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). ʿIkrimah and another group said it is the Night of Acquittal (Laylat al-Bara'a), which is the night of the middle of Sha'ban. As for the first group, they argued for the soundness of their view with several points:
The first: He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1], and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So it must be that this blessed night is that which is called the Night of Power, lest there be contradiction.
The second: He said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], thus clarifying that the sending down of the Qur'an occurred in the month of Ramadan; and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So this blessed night must fall in the month of Ramadan, and everyone who said this blessed night falls in Ramadan said it is the Night of Power; thus it is established that it is the Night of Power.
The third: He said describing the Night of Power: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 4–5]. He also said here: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾, which is appropriate to His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿by permission of their Lord concerning every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 5]. When the descriptions are close, it is necessary to say that one of the two nights is the other.
The fourth: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated in his Tafsir from Qatadah that he said: "The scrolls of Ibrahim were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah on the sixth night of it, the Psalms on the twelfth night that had passed of it, the Gospel on the eighteenth night that had passed of it, and the Qur'an on the twenty-fourth night that had passed of Ramadan; and the blessed night is the Night of Power."
The fifth: The Night of Power was named so because its worth (qadr) and nobility with God is great. It is known that its worth and nobility are not due to that time itself, because time is one thing in its essence and attributes, so it is impossible for some part of it to be more noble than another in its essence. Thus it is established that its nobility and worth are due to the fact that great noble matters occurred in it, which have great worth and a lofty rank. It is known that the rank of religion is higher and greater than the rank of this world, and the highest and most noble of things in religion in rank is the Qur'an, because through it the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ was established, and through it the distinction between truth and falsehood became manifest in all the other revealed books of God, as He said describing it: ("and a guardian over it" [al-Ma'idah: 48]), and through it the degrees of the people of felicity and the depths of the people of wretchedness became manifest. Accordingly, nothing is greater in worth, higher in mention, or greater in rank than the Qur'an. So if its descent had occurred in another night besides the Night of Power, then the Night of Power would be this second night, not the first. And since they agreed that the Night of Power which falls in Ramadan is the one, we know that the Qur'an was sent down in that night.

As for those who say that the blessed night mentioned in this verse is the middle night of Sha'ban, I have not seen for them any proof to rely upon; they have been content merely to transmit it from some people. If there is a saying from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning it, then there is nothing more to be said; otherwise the truth is the first view. Then these proponents of this view claim that the middle night of Sha'ban has four names: the Blessed Night, the Night of Acquittal, the Night of the Decree (Laylat al-Sakk), and the Night of Mercy. It is also said that it was named the Night of Acquittal and the Night of the Decree because when the official (bunduar) collects the land tax from its people, he writes them an acquittal; likewise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes an acquittal for His believing servants on this night. It is also said: this night is specific to five qualities:
The first: the distinguishing of every wise matter therein, as He said: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾.
The second: the excellence of worship in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays one hundred units of prayer on this night, Allah sends to him one hundred angels: thirty to give him good news of Paradise, thirty to secure him from the punishment of the Fire, thirty to ward off the calamities of this world, and ten to ward off the schemes of Satan."
The third quality: the descent of mercy. He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah shows mercy to my community on this night in number equal to the hair of the sheep of the Banu Kalb."
The fourth quality: the attainment of forgiveness. He ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, forgives all Muslims on that night, except a soothsayer, or a person harboring enmity, or a habitual drinker of wine, or one who is disobedient to his parents, or one who persists in fornication."
The fifth quality: that God gave His Messenger on this night the complete intercession. That is, he asked on the thirteenth night of Sha'ban for his community, and was given a third of it; then he asked on the fourteenth night and was given two-thirds; then he asked on the fifteenth night and was given all of it, except whoever fled from God as a camel flees.
I have transmitted this section from the *Kashshaf*. If it is said: there is no doubt that time is an expression for the extended duration whose measure is the motions of the spheres and the stars, and that in itself it is a thing whose parts are alike, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be better than others; and place is an expression for extended space and empty void, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be more noble than others; and if that is so, then specifying some of its parts with greater nobility over the rest is a preference of one side of a possibility over the other without a determining cause, and that is impossible. We say: the affirmation of the createdness of the world and the affirmation that its Agent is a free-choosing agent is based on this principle, namely that it is not improbable for a free-choosing agent to specify a particular time for bringing the world into being rather than what precedes or follows it. If this principle is refuted, then the createdness of the world is refuted and the free-choosing Agent is refuted, and then the discussion of the interpretation of the Qur'an would have no benefit. And if this principle is sound, then the question you raised is removed. This is the reliable answer. People have also said: it is not improbable that God specifies some times with greater honor, so that this becomes an incentive for the responsible person to undertake acts of obedience in that time. For this reason He made it clear that He concealed it among the times and did not specify it; for if it were not specific, the responsible person would suppose in every time that it might be that noble time, and this would move him to persist in acts of obedience at all times. When you reflect on this principle, it becomes clear to you that time and place only gained additional distinctions following the nobility of the human being, who is the principal, and everything else is subordinate to him. And God knows best.

The sixth issue: It is narrated that ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥarūrī asked Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1] and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, how is this valid, given that Allah sent down the Qur'an in all the months? Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "O son of the black woman, if I die and this comes into your mind and you do not find its answer, you are ruined. The Qur'an descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the House of Honor (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), which is in the lowest heaven; then it descended afterward in various events, occasion by occasion." And God knows best.

The seventh issue: explaining the arrangement of these verses. Know that their purpose is the glorification of the Qur'an from three aspects:
The first: the explanation of the glorification of the Qur'an in terms of its own essence.
The second: the explanation of its glorification by reason of the nobility of the time in which it was sent down.

The third aspect: the explanation of its greatness in terms of the nobility of its rank.

As for the explanation of its greatness in terms of its essence, it has three aspects:

The first is that God Most High swore by it, and that indicates its nobility.

The second is that God Most High swore by it regarding its being sent down on a blessed night. We have mentioned that swearing by a thing with regard to one of its own states indicates that it is at the utmost level of nobility.

The third is that God Most High described it as being "clear" (mubin), and that also indicates its nobility in its essence.

As for the second type, which is the explanation of its nobility by virtue of the nobility of the time at which it was sent down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾. This is an alert that its being sent down on a blessed night requires its nobility and majesty. Then we say: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ requires two matters. One is that God Most High sent it down. The second is that this night is blessed. God then mentioned, after this statement, what serves as an explanation of each of the two. As for the explanation of why God Most High sent it down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever warners﴾, meaning that the wisdom in sending down this sura is that the warning of creation is not complete except by it. As for the explanation that this night is a blessed night, there are two matters. One is that God Most High makes every wise matter distinct therein. The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

As for the third type, it is the explanation of the nobility of the Qur'an by virtue of the nobility of its Sender. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾. He thus explained that this warning and sending were brought about only by God Most High. Then He explained that this sending was for the sake of perfecting mercy, which is His saying: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾. The expected phrasing would have been "as a mercy from Us," but He placed the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to signify that lordship (rububiyyah) requires mercy upon those who are nurtured. Then He explained that this mercy fell in accordance with the needs of those in need, because God Most High hears their supplications and knows the kinds of their needs. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This is what came to mind regarding how some of these verses are connected to others.

**Eighth issue: explaining the individual words of these expressions.**

As for His saying Most High: ﴿Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night﴾, it has been said regarding it that God Most High sent down the Qur'an in its entirety from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven on this night, and then He sent down at every time what the responsible person needs. It has also been said: the copying of that from the Preserved Tablet begins on the Night of Acquittal (laylat al-bara'ah), and the completion takes place on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Then the copy of provisions is handed to Mika'il, the copy of wars to Jibril, likewise earthquakes, thunderbolts and landslides, the copy of deeds to Isma'il, the lord of the lowest heaven, who is a great angel, and the copy of calamities to the Angel of Death.

Page 206

As for His saying Most High: ﴿wherein every wise matter is made distinct﴾, meaning, on that blessed night every wise matter is made distinct, that is, it is detailed and clarified, from their saying: "I separated the thing, I separate it, separation (farq) and criterion (furqan)." The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari's commentary) said: it is read as yufarriqu with shaddah, and as yafruqu with the verb ascribed to the agent and kull in the accusative. The one who distinguishes is God, Mighty and Majestic. Zayd ibn Ali read nufarriqu with the nun.

As for His saying: ﴿every wise matter﴾, al-hakim means "possessor of wisdom." This is because God Most High's assigning each person a specific state in terms of lifespan, provision, term, happiness and misery indicates His profound wisdom. Since those acts and decrees indicate the wisdom of their Doer, they are described as wise. This is a metaphorical attribution, because "wise" is in reality an attribute of the one who issues the command, and describing the matter as such is figurative. Then He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾. Regarding the accusative case of His saying ﴿amran﴾ there are two possibilities.

The first is that it is in the accusative by way of specification (ikhtisas). This is because God Most High explained the nobility of those decrees and rulings by describing them as wise, and then increased the explanation of their nobility by saying: "I mean by this matter a matter arising from Us, existing from Our presence, as Our knowledge and governance require."

The second is that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), and in this there are three possibilities:

The first is that it is a circumstantial state of one of the two pronouns in ﴿We sent it down﴾: either of the pronoun of the agent, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ issuing commands with a command, or of the pronoun of the object, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ while it is a command from Us with what must be done.

The third is what Abu Ali al-Farisi related from Abu al-Hasan, may God have mercy on them both: that he took His saying ﴿amran﴾ as a circumstantial state, and the qualified noun (dhu al-hal) is His saying ﴿every wise matter﴾, which is indefinite.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾, meaning: indeed We performed that warning only for the sake of "Indeed We were ever senders," meaning the prophets.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, meaning, for the sake of mercy, so it is in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning that this mercy was truly mercy, because those in need either mention their needs with their tongues or do not mention them. If they mention them, He Most High hears their speech and so knows their needs; and if they do not mention them, He Most High knows them. Thus it is established that His being (All-Hearing, All-Knowing) requires that He send down His mercy upon them.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are certain﴾. There are issues regarding this:

The first issue: Ibn Amir... — *[see note below]*

The first issue: Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "rabbi" with a kasrah on the ba' as an adjunct to His saying ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, while the rest read it with a dammah as an adjunct to His saying ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

The second issue: the purpose of this verse is that when the one who sends down is described with this majesty and greatness, what is sent down, which is the Qur'an, is at the utmost level of nobility and elevation.

The third issue: the benefit of His saying ﴿if you are certain﴾ is of several aspects:

The first: Abu Muslim said: its meaning is, if you seek certainty and desire it, then know that the matter is as We have said, like their saying: "So-and-so is a man of Najd and Tihamah," meaning he intends Najd and Tihamah.

The second: the author of al-Kashshaf said: they used to acknowledge that the heavens and the earth had a Lord and Creator, so it was said to them: the sending of messengers and the sending down of books is a mercy from the Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, then it was said: this is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, whom you acknowledge and admit to be the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if your acknowledgment is from knowledge and certainty, just as you say: "This is the bounty of Zayd, whose generosity people have heard of, if his report has reached you and you have heard his story." Then He Most High rejected that they were certain, by His saying: ﴿Nay, but they are in doubt, playing﴾, and that their acknowledgment does not proceed from knowledge and certainty, nor from earnestness and reality, but is a statement mixed with mockery and play. And God knows best.

The seventh issue: explaining the arrangement of these verses. Know that their purpose is the glorification of the Qur'an from three aspects:

The second: the explanation of its glorification by reason of the nobility of the time in which it was sent down.

The third aspect: the explanation of its greatness in terms of the nobility of its rank.

As for the explanation of its greatness in terms of its essence, it has three aspects:

The first is that God Most High swore by it, and that indicates its nobility.

The second is that God Most High swore by it regarding its being sent down on a blessed night. We have mentioned that swearing by a thing with regard to one of its own states indicates that it is at the utmost level of nobility.

The third is that God Most High described it as being "clear" (mubin), and that also indicates its nobility in its essence.

As for the second type, which is the explanation of its nobility by virtue of the nobility of the time at which it was sent down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾. This is an alert that its being sent down on a blessed night requires its nobility and majesty. Then we say: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ requires two matters. One is that God Most High sent it down. The second is that this night is blessed. God then mentioned, after this statement, what serves as an explanation of each of the two. As for the explanation of why God Most High sent it down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever warners﴾, meaning that the wisdom in sending down this sura is that the warning of creation is not complete except by it. As for the explanation that this night is a blessed night, there are two matters. One is that God Most High makes every wise matter distinct therein. The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

It has also been said: the copying of that from the Preserved Tablet begins on the Night of Acquittal (laylat al-bara'ah), and the completion takes place on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). We have mentioned many times that all these proofs indicate that a thing composed of successive letters and consecutive sounds is created, and knowledge of this is necessary and self-evident; none disputes it except one who lacks reason and does not know the meaning of the eternal and the created. The second is that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), and in this there are three possibilities:

The first is that it is a circumstantial state of one of the two pronouns in ﴿We sent it down﴾: either of the pronoun of the agent, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ issuing commands with a command, or of the pronoun of the object, meaning ﴿Indeed We sent it down﴾ while it is a command from Us with what must be done.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾, meaning: indeed We performed that warning only for the sake of "Indeed We were ever senders," meaning the prophets.

\* \* \*

Then He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, meaning, for the sake of mercy, so it is in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

The first issue: concerning His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ there are several possibilities:
The first: the intended meaning is: this is ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾, like your saying: "This is Zayd, by Allah."
The second: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾, and then it is said: ﴿By the Book that makes things clear.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down.﴾
The third: the intended meaning is: Ha, Mim, by the Book that makes things clear, indeed We sent it down; so this is, in effect, two oaths upon one thing.

The second issue: They said: this indicates that the Qur'an is created (ḥudūth), for several reasons:
The first: His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾, its meaning being: this is Ha, Mim, meaning this is a thing composed of these letters, and what is composed of successive letters is created (muḥdath).
The second: it is established that swearing by these things is not valid, but rather by the Lord of these things; so the meaning is: "By the Lord of Ha, Mim and the Lord of the Clear Book." And whoever is a created being under lordship is created.
The third: He described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from gathering (jam'), so its meaning is that it is gathered, and what is gathered is subject to the handling of others, and whatever is so is created.
The fourth: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, and what is sent down is subject to the handling of others (page 203), and whatever is so is created. We have mentioned many times that all these proofs indicate that a thing composed of successive letters and consecutive sounds is created, and knowledge of this is necessary and self-evident; none disputes it except one who lacks reason and does not know the meaning of the eternal and the created. And if that is so, how could one dispute the soundness of these proofs? What has been established as eternal is something other than what is composed of these letters and sounds.

The third issue: It is possible that by "the Book" here is meant the earlier scriptures which God sent down to His prophets, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39], and He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]. It is also possible that what is meant is the Qur'an; and on this reading He swears by the Qur'an that He sent it down during a blessed night. This kind of speech indicates the utmost glorification of the Qur'an, just as a man may say, when he wishes to exalt a person from whom he needs something: "I seek your intercession with yourself, and I swear by your right over you."

The fourth issue: ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the Clear) is that which includes the explanation of what people need in their religion and their worldly affairs. He described it as "making clear," although the true act of making clear belongs to God, because the clarification was achieved through it, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76], and He said in another verse: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and He said: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate?﴾ [al-Rum: 35]. Thus He described it with speech, since it is the utmost in clarification, so it is as though it were a tongue that speaks; and the purpose in this is to exaggerate its description with this meaning.

The fifth issue: They differed concerning this blessed night. Most said it is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). ʿIkrimah and another group said it is the Night of Acquittal (Laylat al-Bara'a), which is the night of the middle of Sha'ban. As for the first group, they argued for the soundness of their view with several points:
The first: He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1], and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So it must be that this blessed night is that which is called the Night of Power, lest there be contradiction.
The second: He said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], thus clarifying that the sending down of the Qur'an occurred in the month of Ramadan; and here He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾. So this blessed night must fall in the month of Ramadan, and everyone who said this blessed night falls in Ramadan said it is the Night of Power; thus it is established that it is the Night of Power.
The third: He said describing the Night of Power: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 4–5]. He also said here: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾, which is appropriate to His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿a command from Us﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿by permission of their Lord concerning every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. Here He said: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾, and in that verse He said: ﴿Peace it is﴾ [al-Qadr: 5]. When the descriptions are close, it is necessary to say that one of the two nights is the other.
The fourth: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated in his Tafsir from Qatadah that he said: "The scrolls of Ibrahim were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah on the sixth night of it, the Psalms on the twelfth night that had passed of it, the Gospel on the eighteenth night that had passed of it, and the Qur'an on the twenty-fourth night that had passed of Ramadan; and the blessed night is the Night of Power."
The fifth: The Night of Power was named so because its worth (qadr) and nobility with God is great. It is known that its worth and nobility are not due to that time itself, because time is one thing in its essence and attributes, so it is impossible for some part of it to be more noble than another in its essence. Thus it is established that its nobility and worth are due to the fact that great noble matters occurred in it, which have great worth and a lofty rank. It is known that the rank of religion is higher and greater than the rank of this world, and the highest and most noble of things in religion in rank is the Qur'an, because through it the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ was established, and through it the distinction between truth and falsehood became manifest in all the other revealed books of God, as He said describing it: ("and a guardian over it" [al-Ma'idah: 48]), and through it the degrees of the people of felicity and the depths of the people of wretchedness became manifest. Accordingly, nothing is greater in worth, higher in mention, or greater in rank than the Qur'an. So if its descent had occurred in another night besides the Night of Power, then the Night of Power would be this second night, not the first. And since they agreed that the Night of Power which falls in Ramadan is the one, we know that the Qur'an was sent down in that night.

As for those who say that the blessed night mentioned in this verse is the middle night of Sha'ban, I have not seen for them any proof to rely upon; they have been content merely to transmit it from some people. If there is a saying from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning it, then there is nothing more to be said; otherwise the truth is the first view. Then these proponents of this view claim that the middle night of Sha'ban has four names: the Blessed Night, the Night of Acquittal, the Night of the Decree (Laylat al-Sakk), and the Night of Mercy. It is also said that it was named the Night of Acquittal and the Night of the Decree because when the official (bunduar) collects the land tax from its people, he writes them an acquittal; likewise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes an acquittal for His believing servants on this night. It is also said: this night is specific to five qualities:
The first: the distinguishing of every wise matter therein, as He said: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾.
The second: the excellence of worship in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays one hundred units of prayer on this night, Allah sends to him one hundred angels: thirty to give him good news of Paradise, thirty to secure him from the punishment of the Fire, thirty to ward off the calamities of this world, and ten to ward off the schemes of Satan."
The third quality: the descent of mercy. He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah shows mercy to my community on this night in number equal to the hair of the sheep of the Banu Kalb."
The fourth quality: the attainment of forgiveness. He ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, forgives all Muslims on that night, except a soothsayer, or a person harboring enmity, or a habitual drinker of wine, or one who is disobedient to his parents, or one who persists in fornication."
The fifth quality: that God gave His Messenger on this night the complete intercession. That is, he asked on the thirteenth night of Sha'ban for his community, and was given a third of it; then he asked on the fourteenth night and was given two-thirds; then he asked on the fifteenth night and was given all of it, except whoever fled from God as a camel flees.
I have transmitted this section from the *Kashshaf*. If it is said: there is no doubt that time is an expression for the extended duration whose measure is the motions of the spheres and the stars, and that in itself it is a thing whose parts are alike, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be better than others; and place is an expression for extended space and empty void, so it is impossible for some of its parts to be more noble than others; and if that is so, then specifying some of its parts with greater nobility over the rest is a preference of one side of a possibility over the other without a determining cause, and that is impossible. We say: the affirmation of the createdness of the world and the affirmation that its Agent is a free-choosing agent is based on this principle, namely that it is not improbable for a free-choosing agent to specify a particular time for bringing the world into being rather than what precedes or follows it. If this principle is refuted, then the createdness of the world is refuted and the free-choosing Agent is refuted, and then the discussion of the interpretation of the Qur'an would have no benefit. And if this principle is sound, then the question you raised is removed. This is the reliable answer. People have also said: it is not improbable that God specifies some times with greater honor, so that this becomes an incentive for the responsible person to undertake acts of obedience in that time. For this reason He made it clear that He concealed it among the times and did not specify it; for if it were not specific, the responsible person would suppose in every time that it might be that noble time, and this would move him to persist in acts of obedience at all times. When you reflect on this principle, it becomes clear to you that time and place only gained additional distinctions following the nobility of the human being, who is the principal, and everything else is subordinate to him. And God knows best.

The sixth issue: It is narrated that ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥarūrī asked Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power﴾ [al-Qadr: 1] and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, how is this valid, given that Allah sent down the Qur'an in all the months? Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "O son of the black woman, if I die and this comes into your mind and you do not find its answer, you are ruined. And God knows best.

* * *

The seventh issue: explaining the arrangement of these verses. Know that their purpose is the glorification of the Qur'an from three aspects:
The first: the explanation of the glorification of the Qur'an in terms of its own essence.
The second: the explanation of its glorification by reason of the nobility of the time in which it was sent down.

The third aspect: the explanation of its greatness in terms of the nobility of its rank.

As for the explanation of its greatness in terms of its essence, it has three aspects:

The first is that God Most High swore by it, and that indicates its nobility.

The second is that God Most High swore by it regarding its being sent down on a blessed night. We have mentioned that swearing by a thing with regard to one of its own states indicates that it is at the utmost level of nobility.

The third is that God Most High described it as being "clear" (mubin), and that also indicates its nobility in its essence.

As for the second type, which is the explanation of its nobility by virtue of the nobility of the time at which it was sent down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾. This is an alert that its being sent down on a blessed night requires its nobility and majesty. Then we say: His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ requires two matters. One is that God Most High sent it down. The second is that this night is blessed. God then mentioned, after this statement, what serves as an explanation of each of the two. As for the explanation of why God Most High sent it down, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever warners﴾, meaning that the wisdom in sending down this sura is that the warning of creation is not complete except by it. As for the explanation that this night is a blessed night, there are two matters. One is that God Most High makes every wise matter distinct therein. The second is that this wise matter is distinguished by the nobility that it manifests only from His presence, and to this is the allusion in His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾.

As for the third type, it is the explanation of the nobility of the Qur'an by virtue of the nobility of its Sender. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed We were ever senders﴾. He thus explained that this warning and sending were brought about only by God Most High. Then He explained that this sending was for the sake of perfecting mercy, which is His saying: ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾. The expected phrasing would have been "as a mercy from Us," but He placed the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to signify that lordship (rububiyyah) requires mercy upon those who are nurtured. Then He explained that this mercy fell in accordance with the needs of those in need, because God Most High hears their supplications and knows the kinds of their needs. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This is what came to mind regarding how some of these verses are connected to others.

As for His saying Most High: ﴿Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night﴾, it has been said regarding it that God Most High sent down the Qur'an in its entirety from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven on this night, and then He sent down at every time what the responsible person needs.
